purpose: Durable ownership map for the CLI source tree. The architecture conformance suite requires every top-level source entry to appear in exactly one component; new modules need an explicit owner, not an implicit one. This file records architecture responsibility, not release approval or contributor policy (AGENTS.md owns policy).

components.responsibility: Process entry, argument dispatch, command registration, daemon and lite startup. Owns the executable boundary; no domain decisions.

ChatEngine loop, task admission, tool proposal/execution glue and completion-gate policy. Cross-cutting: admission (W01), completion (W02), context (W05) and tool contracts (W06) all meet here, so edits need the owning issue.
Mode-neutral executor contracts, completion decision, effect classification, verifier stages and criterion authority. Normative behavior lives in docs/architecture/HARNESS_ARCHITECTURE_V1.md.
Governed deep pipeline, stage sequencing, checkpoint/rollback and orchestrator routing. Hot path: pipeline.ts stays a coordination surface, not a second tool catalog.
Run control, event projection, recovery/restore reports and evidence recording. Terminal honesty decisions stay with completion-kernel.
Tool catalog, adapters, MCP bridge, local tools and shell output normalization. Mode/approval restrictions are contract owners' decisions; adapters must not widen them.
Sandbox profiles, container lifecycle, file-write boundaries, process-tree termination and portable workflow execution.
TUI rendering, input ownership, REPL/session UX and transcript presentation. rendererSupport.ts and conversationalRenderer.ts own the live output path; raw stdout is boundary-registered, not ad hoc.
Resolver/compiler, catalog parsing, routing, model policy, research and search ingestion. prompt_catalog.yaml owns routes; runtime contracts stay in completion-kernel.
Shared service layer: reviews, readiness, workspace transactions, verifier contracts, cost/telemetry-adjacent services and operator maintenance audits.
Execute-mode entry, evaluation harnesses, budgets, calibration and acceptance fixtures. Owns scoring and measurement, not runtime completion authority.
Doctor/installed-doctor checks, diagnostic streams, BDNS observation and repository audit reports. Diagnostics observe; they do not certify completion.
Provider adapters and request/response translation. Offline fixtures and capability facts are owned here; credential custody stays in the sandbox/security boundary.
OpenTelemetry tracing/span schema plus voice capture and keybinding plumbing. Emission is subordinate to runtime authority and must not leak prompt or credential payloads.
Runtime configuration resolution and shared schemas. Schema changes co-evolve with their consumer contract and need serialized integration review.
Small dependency-free helpers shared across components. Not a home for new domain logic.
Test harness, ambient-inference isolation, fixtures and tracing helpers. Product behavior belongs to the component under test.
